card.name: Verbs of when an event occurs in treatment
card.fires_on: The verb "occur" (occurred, occurs) or a nearby word like "early", "as" or "day", right before a time point in treatment such as "during the first three months" or "within 30 minutes". It marks where a time-of-onset phrase is about to follow.

modes.label: Occur before onset time
modes.description: Forms of "occur" in statements about when an adverse reaction or effect happens relative to treatment.
modes.example: Isoniazid-associated hepatitis usually<< occurs>> during the first three months of treatment.

modes.label: Early/as/day before a time
modes.description: Words like "early", "as" in "as early as", or "day" that lead into a specific time point.
modes.example: The LDL-lowering effect of PRALUENT may be measured as early<< as>> 4 weeks after initiation.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward time-span words such as "six months", "three months", "third" and "over time" (including Chinese ones).
card.plain: It fires on words that say when something happens in treatment, just before a time like "within 3 months" is given.
